mainTopic: Exceptions to 'כאשר זמם' for עדים זוממין: גלות, מלקות, כופר, being sold as an עבד עברי, and paying on one's own admission
overview: The amud opens by finishing the בן גרושה discussion. A קל וחומר is rejected, and the גמרא goes back to its first answer from the פסוק. Next, ריש לקיש learns from the word 'הוא' that עדים זוממין who said someone owes גלות are not exiled. רבי יוחנן's קל וחומר fails, because גלות is a כפרה. עולא then finds a hint in the Torah that עדים זוממין can get מלקות: 'והצדיקו את הצדיק והרשיעו את הרשע'. That hint is needed because 'לא תענה' has no action, so it cannot bring lashes. A ברייתא lists four punishments that עדים זוממין do not receive, and the גמרא explains them one by one. On כופר, רב חסדא and רב פפא argue about whether כופר is atonement or how it is measured. On being sold as an עבד עברי, רבא uses 'בגנבתו' to reject both versions of רב המנונא's limit. Finally, רבי עקיבא exempts witnesses who admit they were caught, because their payment is a קנס. רבה and רב נחמן each prove it is a קנס.

steps.title: The earlier logic would mean עדים זוממין are never stoned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the earlier קל וחומר by showing that the same reasoning would cancel stoning for עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If witnesses whose victim was actually stoned are not stoned themselves, then witnesses who only tried to get him stoned should surely not be stoned either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to an earlier קל וחומר. It shows that the same style of reasoning leads to a result we know is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: if the victim was already executed, the עדים זוממין are not executed. If we follow the earlier קל וחומר, witnesses who failed to get him killed should be let off as well. But the תורה clearly says those witnesses ARE punished, so this kind of קל וחומר cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who 'stoned': witnesses whose victim was actually executed by stoning
the one who tried to get someone stoned but did not succeed
isn't it logical? (the standard opening for the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is NOT saying that עדים זוממין really go free. It builds this absurd conclusion on purpose, to show that the earlier קל וחומר is broken.

phrases.english: If one who 'stoned' is not stoned,
phrases.notes: These are witnesses whose victim was already executed before they were caught lying. They are not executed.

phrases.english: then one who came to stone but did not stone —
isn't it logical that he should not be stoned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge, from just before this section, against the קל וחומר about witnesses who tried to make a כהן into a בן גרושה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier קל וחומר: if the one who actually disqualified a כהן is not disqualified, then the one who only tried should not be either.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum. The same form of reasoning would cancel stoning for עדים זוממין, which goes against the תורה.

steps.title: Back to the original answer from the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the קל וחומר and returns to its first explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear, as we answered at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the קל וחומר failed, the גמרא goes back to the answer it gave at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer came from the פסוק, not from logic. 'וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ' means 'to him, not to his children.' And 'כאשר זמם' requires carrying out the whole plot, so we cannot disqualify the witness alone either. So the witnesses do not become חללים at all; they get lashes instead.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear (the גמרא is settling on an answer after rejecting another)
as we answered at first

steps.whatToRemember: The rule about the בן גרושה case rests on the פסוק ('to him, not to his children', and the plot must be carried out in full), not on a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at the start.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier answer from the פסוק (דברים 19:19): it's 'to him,' not his children, and the plot is done in full or not at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because step 1 knocked down the קל וחומר, the גמרא goes back to the source from the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source for not making the witnesses into חללים is the פסוק, not a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the exile case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and asks where we know it from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'We testify that so-and-so owes גלות' (the witnesses are not exiled). Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, about false witnesses who said someone must go into גלות. It asks for the source of the rule that the witnesses are not exiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally עדים זוממין receive exactly what they tried to do to the other person. Here the משנה makes an exception: they get lashes instead of גלות. The גמרא wants to know what source makes this exception.

keyTerms.meaning: must go into exile to an עיר מקלט (for killing someone by accident)
so-and-so, a certain person
from where do we know these words? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: 'We testify about so-and-so
that he is liable to exile,' etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה: the witnesses aren't exiled in his place, and they get forty lashes instead.

phrases.english: From where are these words derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the בן גרושה case to the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that עדים זוממין who said someone owes גלות are not exiled themselves.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'He' flees, not the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the rule from the word 'הוא' in the פסוק about the accidental killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: the פסוק says 'He shall flee to one of the cities.' 'He' means the killer, and not the עדים זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question with a פסוק. The word 'He' limits גלות to the actual killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just described the flight. The extra word 'הוא' tells us that only the real killer goes to an עיר מקלט. Witnesses who lied about a killing are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: a פסוק, a verse
he shall flee
the cities, meaning the ערי מקלט (cities of refuge)
plotting false witnesses who were proven false by הזמה

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
As the verse says:
"He shall flee to one of the cities" —
phrases.notes: דברים 19:5

phrases.english: He, and not conspiring witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'הוא' in the פסוק limits גלות to the killer himself and leaves out עדים זוממין.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a logical argument instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן offers a קל וחומר: if a killer who acted on purpose is not exiled, witnesses who did no act certainly are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it comes from a קל וחומר. A killer actually did something, and if he did it on purpose he is not exiled. The witnesses did not actually do anything, even if they lied on purpose. Isn't it logical that they are not exiled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different source, using logic instead of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גלות applies only to accidental killing, never to a killer who acted on purpose. The witnesses lied on purpose, and they did not even carry out an act of killing. So רבי יוחנן reasons that they are even further from גלות than an intentional killer.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
a physical act (here, actually killing someone)
on purpose, intentionally
goes into exile

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: it is an a fortiori argument:
If he, who did an act —
if done intentionally, is not exiled,
then they, who did not do an act —
acting intentionally, isn't it logical that they should not be exiled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logical source instead of ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: an intentional killer is not exiled, so intentional witnesses who did no act should surely not be exiled.

steps.title: The logic actually points the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי יוחנן's קל וחומר, because גלות is a כפרה that the less guilty witnesses may deserve.
steps.simpleTranslation: That very point works the opposite way. The intentional killer is not exiled so that he gets no כפרה. The witnesses did no act, so they should be exiled, so that they do get a כפרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's argument. It shows that the same facts can support the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not exiling an intentional killer is not a lighter treatment. Being exiled would actually be a כפרה, and he is too guilty to deserve it. The witnesses are less guilty, since they did no act, so maybe they deserve the כפרה of גלות. That breaks the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: that very reason gives the opposite result
atonement
so that
let them be exiled

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think of גלות here only as a punishment. In this argument it is a כפרה, and that is exactly why a worse sinner might NOT get it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: גלות works as a כפרה, not only as a penalty. That is why 'no גלות' can be the harsher outcome.

phrases.english: But that very point gives the opposite: (and isn't it logical?):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: he, who did an act —
if intentional, let him not be exiled,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא תֶּיהְוֵי לֵיהּ כַּפָּרָה.
phrases.english: so that he will not have atonement.
They, who did not do an act —
even if intentional, let them also be exiled,
so that they will have atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן's קל וחומר from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר of רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קל וחומר treats 'no גלות' as the lighter outcome. But גלות is a כפרה, so an intentional sinner is denied it, while the less guilty witnesses might deserve it.

steps.title: Settling on ריש לקיש's verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the source is ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the source is like ריש לקיש said.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the קל וחומר failed, the גמרא accepts ריש לקיש's source from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone could go either way, so we need the פסוק. 'הוא', meaning 'he and not the עדים זוממין', is what keeps the witnesses out of גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (dropping the previous idea)
in line with, like

steps.whatToRemember: עדים זוממין who said someone owes גלות are not exiled. The source is the פסוק 'הוא ינוס', not a קל וחומר, because גלות is a כפרה and logic could cut both ways.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear as Reish Lakish said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 rejects רבי יוחנן's logic, the גמרא returns to ריש לקיש from step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק 'הוא ינוס אל אחת הערים' teaches that only the killer, and not עדים זוממין, goes into גלות.

steps.title: עולא asks where the Torah hints at conspiring witnesses
steps.stepSummary: עולא opens a new topic by asking for a hint in the Torah for עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: Where does the Torah hint at conspiring witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. עולא asks where the Torah hints at עדים זוממין, which are witnesses proven false because other witnesses showed they were somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'רמז' is a hint, not a full open teaching. As worded, the question seems odd, and the גמרא will challenge it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint or allusion in a פסוק
Plotting witnesses: false witnesses caught because other witnesses say 'you were with us somewhere else'
From the Torah itself

phrases.english: Ulla says:
An allusion to conspiring witnesses
from the Torah, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: רֶמֶז לְעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of exile ended in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah hint for the law of עדים זוממין.

steps.title: There is already a clear verse for conspiring witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: why look for a hint when the Torah says it openly?
steps.simpleTranslation: A hint for conspiring witnesses?! But it is written openly: 'And you shall do to him as he conspired'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on עולא's question. The Torah already says the law of עדים זוממין clearly, so why would anyone need a hint?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם' openly teaches that false witnesses get what they plotted to do. So עולא's question, as worded, cannot be what he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it...': a word that opens a challenge
'As he plotted': the false witness receives what he planned to do to the accused

phrases.english: An allusion to conspiring witnesses?!
But isn't it written:
"And you shall do to him as he conspired"!
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of עולא's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no need for a hint, because there is an open פסוק about עדים זוממין.

steps.title: Reframing: the hint is for lashing conspiring witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that עולא was asking about מלקות for עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: Where does the Torah hint that conspiring witnesses are given lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes עולא's question. He was not asking about עדים זוממין in general. He was asking where we see that they can get מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כאשר זמם' only teaches that they get what they plotted. In some cases they cannot get the plotted punishment, and then they get lashes instead. That lashing rule needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the earlier reading and offers a new one
They receive lashes
The punishment of lashes

phrases.english: Rather:
an allusion to conspiring witnesses who are flogged
from the Torah, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רֶמֶז לְעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין שֶׁלּוֹקִין מִן הַתּוֹרָה, מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9 by narrowing עולא's question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא was asking for any hint about עדים זוממין.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא was asking specifically about מלקות for עדים זוממין.

steps.title: The verse about vindicating the righteous
steps.stepSummary: עולא brings the פסוק 'וְהִצְדִּיקוּ אֶת הַצַּדִּיק' as the hint for lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they vindicated the righteous and condemned the wicked. And it shall be, if the wicked deserves lashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives his source: a פסוק about judges declaring one side right and the other wrong, followed by lashes for the guilty one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the פסוק itself. How it connects to עדים זוממין is not yet clear, and the גמרא will now ask about that.

keyTerms.meaning: They declared him righteous (in the right)
They declared him wicked (guilty)
Deserving of lashes

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And they vindicated the righteous
and condemned the wicked.
And it shall be if the wicked is deserving of lashes."
phrases.notes: דברים 25:1–2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the reframed question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דברים 25 about vindicating the righteous and lashing the wicked.

steps.title: Why would vindicating one side mean lashes for the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוק, read simply, does not make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because they vindicated the righteous and condemned the wicked, does that mean the wicked one gets lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the plain reading of the פסוק. In most court cases, winning or losing does not lead to lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two people argue about money and one loses, he pays. He is not lashed. So the פסוק must be talking about a special case, and the גמרא is setting up its explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
Here: the side that is found to be in the right
Here: the side that is found guilty

phrases.english: Because "they vindicated the righteous" –
"they condemned the wicked,
and it shall be if the wicked is deserving of lashes"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the פסוק from step 11 should be read.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Losing a court case does not normally bring lashes, so the plain reading cannot be right.

steps.title: The verse describes false witnesses exposed by other witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is about witnesses who falsely accused an innocent man and were then proven to be עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: witnesses made an innocent man look guilty. Other witnesses came, cleared the original innocent man, and made these first witnesses the wicked ones. About them it says: 'And it shall be, if the wicked deserves lashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק as a case of עדים זוממין. The 'righteous' is the accused man, and the 'wicked' are the false witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second witnesses clear the accused, and that same act makes the first witnesses guilty. This is the only case where clearing one person directly causes another to be lashed. So the פסוק is the hint that עדים זוממין can receive מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Others (Aramaic)
From the beginning; the original one
They made them into

steps.confusionAlert: The 'רשע' who gets lashes is not the accused man. It is the first set of witnesses. The 'צדיק' is the accused man they lied about.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for lashing עדים זוממין is 'וְהִצְדִּיקוּ אֶת הַצַּדִּיק וְהִרְשִׁיעוּ אֶת הָרָשָׁע', read as a case of witnesses proven false by other witnesses.

phrases.english: Rather: witnesses who condemned the righteous,
and other witnesses came
and vindicated the original righteous one,
and rendered these wicked,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the first witnesses, who are now shown to be liars.

phrases.english: "and it shall be if the wicked is deserving of lashes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty from step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק talks about any court case between two people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק talks about עדים זוממין exposed by a second set of witnesses.

steps.title: Why not learn lashes from 'You shall not bear false witness'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need this hint when there is a clear לאו against false testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not learn it from 'You shall not bear false witness'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for עולא's source. Breaking a לאו normally brings lashes, and false witnesses broke the לאו of 'לֹא תַעֲנֶה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לֹא תַעֲנֶה' already brings lashes, the hidden hint from דברים 25 seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it': why not learn it from an easier source?
The prohibition against giving false testimony
A negative commandment

phrases.english: And let him derive it from "You shall not bear"!
phrases.notes: שמות 20:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the source in step 13 is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain לאו against false testimony should already bring lashes.

steps.title: A prohibition without an action does not bring lashes
steps.stepSummary: 'לֹא תַעֲנֶה' is broken through speech alone, so it cannot bring lashes. That is why the hint is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a prohibition that involves no action, and for any prohibition that involves no action, one is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that false testimony is done only with words. The rule is that a לאו broken without a physical act does not bring מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'לֹא תַעֲנֶה' cannot bring lashes by itself, we need a special source to teach that עדים זוממין are lashed. That source is the פסוק עולא brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment that is broken without doing a physical act
One does not get lashes for it

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a לאו without an action does not bring lashes comes up across ש״ס. Here it explains why עדים זוממין need their own special source for מלקות.

phrases.english: Because it is
a prohibition that does not involve an action,
and every prohibition that does not involve an action,
one is not flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a general rule that blocks the alternative source
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לֹא תַעֲנֶה' has no action, so it cannot bring lashes. The special hint is needed.

steps.title: Four cases where conspiring witnesses are not punished as they plotted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four punishments that are not given to עדים זוממין, even though they tried to bring them on the accused.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Four things were said about conspiring witnesses. They are not made a son of a divorced woman or a son of a חלוצה. They are not exiled to cities of refuge. They do not pay the ransom. They are not sold as a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with four exceptions. In each case, עדים זוממין do not get the exact punishment they tried to cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally עדים זוממין get 'כאשר זמם', exactly what they plotted. These four are exceptions within that law, not a sign that the witnesses stop being עדים זוממין. We already saw the exile case in steps 3-7, and the גמרא will explain the others next.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן born from a forbidden marriage, who loses his כהונה status
Cities of refuge for accidental killers
Ransom payment owed when a warned ox kills a person
A Jew sold into servitude, for example a thief who cannot repay
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Four matters were stated with regard to conspiring witnesses:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נַעֲשִׂין בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: they are not rendered the son of a divorced woman or the son of a חלוצה,
phrases.notes: If they falsely said a כהן was born from a forbidden marriage, they themselves do not lose their כהונה.

phrases.english: and they are not exiled to cities of refuge,
and they do not pay the ransom,
and they are not sold as a Hebrew slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that lists exceptions in the law of עדים זוממין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In four cases, עדים זוממין do not receive the punishment they plotted: loss of כהונה status for children, exile, כופר, and being sold as an עבד עברי.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: they do not pay based on their own admission
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds that עדים זוממין who admit they were proven false do not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי עקיבא they said: They also do not pay based on their own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds רבי עקיבא's view. If עדים זוממין admit on their own that they were proven false, they do not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment by עדים זוממין only comes from being exposed by other witnesses in court. Their own admission is not enough to make them pay. The גמרא will discuss this view next.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on their own admission
Also; adds one more item to the list

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists four exceptions in the punishment of עדים זוממין, and רבי עקיבא adds a fifth: they do not pay based on their own admission.

phrases.english: They said in the name of Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵין מְשַׁלְּמִין עַל פִּי עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: They also do not pay based on their own admission.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אָמְרוּ: אַף אֵין מְשַׁלְּמִין עַל פִּי עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth exception to the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, עדים זוממין do not pay on the basis of their own admission.

steps.title: Two items in the ברייתא were already explained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes through the ברייתא. It notes that the rules about בן גרושה and exile were already explained earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not made a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, as we already said. They are not sent to cities of refuge, as we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא from step 16 one item at a time. For the first two items, it simply says, 'we already explained this.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of these punishments were already discussed earlier on the דף, so the גמרא does not repeat the reasons. It is clearing the way to explain the item that is new, כופר.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said (already explained earlier)
Cities of refuge
Son of a woman released through חליצה (disqualified from כהונה)

phrases.english: They are not made a son of a divorced woman
or a son of a חלוצה, as we said.
And they are not exiled to cities of refuge,
as we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the items in the ברייתא of step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rules about בן גרושה/חלוצה and exile were already explained earlier.

steps.title: Why the witnesses do not pay כופר
steps.stepSummary: עדים זוממין do not pay כופר, because the ברייתא holds that כופר is atonement, and they need none.
steps.simpleTranslation: They don't pay the ransom, because they hold that the ransom is atonement, and these witnesses are not people who need atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third item: why עדים זוממין who tried to make someone pay כופר do not pay it themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כופר is paid by an owner whose ox killed a person. The ברייתא holds that this payment is a כפרה for the owner, not just a money payment. The witnesses' ox never killed anyone, so they have nothing to atone for, and there is nothing to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom paid by an owner whose ox killed a person
Atonement
They hold (this is their view)
People who need atonement

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of whether כופר is atonement or ordinary payment. The rest of this section is about that question.

phrases.english: And they do not pay the ransom,
because they hold: the ransom is atonement,
and these are not people who need atonement.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the עדים זוממין. Their ox never killed anyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the ברייתא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין do not pay כופר, because כופר is atonement and they need none.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that כופר is atonement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the source is for the view that כופר is atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught that the ransom is atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view the ברייתא relied on. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that כופר is atonement, and not ordinary money, is not obvious. So the גמרא wants to know which known opinion it matches.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (who taught this)?

phrases.english: Who taught that the ransom is atonement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the reasoning given in step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that כופר is atonement

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא points to a ברייתא where the רבנן say כופר is the victim's value, and רבי ישמעאל says it is the damager's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. As a ברייתא teaches: 'He shall give the redemption of his soul' means the value of the victim. רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: the value of the one who caused the damage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the view belongs to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. He brings a ברייתא where the רבנן and רבי ישמעאל argue about how much כופר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say the owner pays what the victim was worth. רבי ישמעאל says he pays what he himself, the owner, is worth. רב חסדא will explain in the next step why this argument shows that רבי ישמעאל holds כופר is atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: The redemption of his soul
The value of the victim
The value of the one who caused the damage

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא,
phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
as it is taught: "And he shall give the redemption of his soul":
phrases.notes: שמות 21:30

phrases.english: the value of the victim.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
the value of the one who caused the damage.
phrases.notes: He means the ox's owner, who pays based on his own worth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view is רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, based on a ברייתא about how כופר is valued.

steps.title: How the ברייתא shows their real disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the רבנן hold כופר is money, and רבי ישמעאל holds it is atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One holds the ransom is a money payment, and the other holds the ransom is atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא proves רב חסדא's point. It reads the argument as being about what כופר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying the victim's value sounds like paying back a loss, so it is money. Paying your own value sounds like redeeming your own life, so it is atonement. That would make רבי ישמעאל the source for 'כופר is atonement.'

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (opens a suggested reading)
They disagree
Money (an ordinary payment)

phrases.english: Isn't it that they disagree about this?
That one master holds: the ransom is money,
phrases.notes: 'One master' here is the רבנן, who said the victim's value.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: the ransom is atonement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא in step 21 supports רב חסדא
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל holds כופר is atonement
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's argument over the victim's value versus the damager's value

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees כופר is atonement
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof. Both sides hold כופר is atonement, and they only argue about whose value we measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: No. Everyone agrees the ransom is atonement. Here they argue about this: one holds we measure by the victim's value, and the other holds we measure by the damager's value.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the proof from step 22. He says the ברייתא does not show the רבנן disagree about atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, everyone agrees about what כופר is. The only question is how it is measured. So the ברייתא is no proof that the רבנן see כופר as money, and the view of our ברייתא need not belong to רבי ישמעאל alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
We assess / measure the value

steps.confusionAlert: Even the רבנן, who measure by the victim's value, can still hold that כופר is atonement. How a payment is measured is a separate question from what kind of payment it is.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: No,
everyone agrees the ransom is atonement,
and here they disagree about this:
one master holds: we assess by the victim's value,
and the other master holds: we assess by the damager's value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading offered in step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא shows an argument over whether כופר is atonement
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be only about how כופר is measured, with both sides agreeing it is atonement.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, everyone holds כופר is atonement. The argument is only whether we measure it by the victim's value or the damager's value.

steps.title: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן measure by the victim's value, when the פסוק says 'his soul.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the רבנן's view. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'פדיון נפשו', 'redemption of his soul', sound like they mean the owner's own value. So the גמרא wants to know what pushed the רבנן to measure by the victim instead.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבנן's view in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן measure כופר by the victim's value

steps.title: The word השתה links כופר to the miscarriage case
steps.stepSummary: The word השתה appears in both the כופר case and the miscarriage case. Just as the miscarriage payment follows the victim's value, so does כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Imposing' is said below, and 'imposing' is said above. Just as there it goes by the victim's value, so too here it goes by the victim's value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source. It links two פסוקים that both use the word השתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of a person who causes a woman to miscarry, the payment is clearly based on the victim, the unborn baby. Because the same word השתה appears in the כופר פסוק, the רבנן learn that כופר is also based on the victim's value.

keyTerms.meaning: Imposing (placing a payment on someone)
Below / above (later and earlier in the פרשה)
Just as there, so too here (a word-link comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן learn from the shared word השתה that כופר is measured by the victim's value, just like the miscarriage payment.

phrases.english: 'Imposing' is stated below,
phrases.notes: 'Below' is the ox case: 'If a ransom is imposed on him' (שמות 21:30).

phrases.english: and 'imposing' is stated above.
phrases.notes: 'Above' is the miscarriage case (שמות 21:22).

phrases.english: Just as there, it is by the victim's value,
so too here, it is by the victim's value.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר הֲשָׁתָה לְמַטָּה, וְנֶאֱמַר הֲשָׁתָה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A word-link (גזירה שוה) on השתה ties כופר to the miscarriage payment, which follows the victim's value.

steps.title: The Source for רבי ישמעאל's View
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל measures כופר by the damager's value because the פסוק says 'the redemption of his soul.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? He points out that the פסוק says 'And he shall give the redemption of his soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last step gave the רבנן's source for measuring by the victim's value. Now the גמרא explains how רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל focuses on the words 'פדיון נפשו', the redemption of HIS soul. Since the owner of the ox is the one redeeming himself, the price is set by his own value, meaning the damager's value.

keyTerms.meaning: The redemption of his soul. The wording of the כופר פסוק.
The atonement payment made by the owner of an ox that killed a person.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael reasons:
'And he shall give the redemption of his soul' is written.
phrases.notes: שמות 21:30

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's source, after step 25 gave the רבנן's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'פדיון נפשו' show that the damager's own value is what counts.

steps.title: How the רבנן Handle 'His Soul'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן agree the payment redeems the damager's soul, but the amount is still measured by the victim's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Yes, 'redemption of his soul' is written. But when we assess the amount, we assess it by the victim's value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with רבי ישמעאל's words. They accept the words but separate what the payment does from how it is measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, 'פדיון נפשו' tells us the purpose of the payment: it redeems the damager. The amount, however, comes from the השתה comparison in step 25, which points to the victim's value.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes. An Aramaic word of agreement.
We assess or appraise a value.
The injured party, the victim.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree כופר is atonement. They argue only about whose value sets the price: the victim's (רבנן) or the damager's (רבי ישמעאל).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? Yes,
'redemption of his soul' is written,
but when we assess the amount,
we assess it by the victim's value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how the רבנן deal with the פסוק רבי ישמעאל relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do the רבנן explain the words 'פדיון נפשו'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words describe the purpose of the payment. The amount is measured by the victim's value.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כופר discussion ends with both sides holding it is atonement and differing only on the measurement.

steps.title: רב המנונא Limits the No-Slavery Rule
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא suggests that עדים זוממין avoid being sold only if the accused person had money. If he had none, they are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says they are not sold as an עבד עברי. רב המנונא wanted to say: this applies only where the accused man has money of his own. Since he would not have been sold, they are not sold either. But if he has no money, they are sold, even if they themselves have money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's rule that עדים זוממין are not sold as an עבד עברי. רב המנונא proposes a limit on that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief who cannot repay is sold as an עבד עברי. רב המנונא reasons that the witnesses get what they tried to do to him. If the accused had money, he would never have been sold, so they are not sold. If he had no money, they tried to get him sold, so they are sold even if they could pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish servant. A thief who cannot pay back what he stole is sold as one.
Scheming witnesses who are proven false and receive the punishment they planned for the accused.
This applies only to... A phrase that limits a rule.
Since. Here: since he would not have been sold.

phrases.english: And they are not sold as a Hebrew slave.
Rav Hamnuna thought to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: This applies only where he himself has money,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man they falsely accused of stealing.

phrases.english: since he would not have been sold,
they too are not sold.
But where he himself does not have money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לְהוּ לְדִידְהוּ – מִיזְדַּבְּנוּ.
phrases.english: even though they have money, they are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the ברייתא: עדים זוממין and the rule about being sold as an עבד עברי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The no-sale rule applies only when the accused had money. If he had none, the witnesses are sold even if they can pay.

steps.title: רבא: The Witnesses Can Answer Back
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that witnesses who have money can say: you would not have been sold if you had money, so neither are we.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But let the witnesses say to him: If you had money, would you have been sold? We have money too, so we will not be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב המנונא's first version. He argues it makes no sense to sell witnesses who are able to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a real thief is sold only when he cannot pay. Witnesses who have money are in the same position as a thief who has money, so they should not be sold either. This breaks the case where the accused is poor but the witnesses are rich.

keyTerms.meaning: But let them say to him. Introduces an argument the other side could make.
Would it have been? A question form expecting the answer no.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But let the witnesses say to him:
If you had money,
would you have been sold?
We too will not be sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's first version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that rich witnesses are sold when the accused was poor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A thief is sold only when he cannot pay. Witnesses who can pay should not be treated worse than a thief who can pay.

steps.title: רב המנונא's Revised Version
steps.stepSummary: A new version of רב המנונא: the witnesses are sold only when neither the accused nor the witnesses have money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב המנונא wanted to say: the rule applies only where either the accused or the witnesses have money. But where neither he nor they have money, the witnesses are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא withdraws the first version of רב המנונא and gives a narrower one that avoids רבא's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the witnesses are sold only when two things are true: the accused would really have been sold, and the witnesses themselves cannot pay. This answers רבא, because rich witnesses are never sold under this version.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the earlier version is dropped for a new one.
Neither to him nor to them.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Hamnuna thought to say:
This applies only where there is money
either to him or to them,
but where there is no money
neither to him nor to them, they are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first version of רב המנונא after רבא's objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses are sold whenever the accused was poor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses are sold only when the accused was poor and they are poor too.

steps.title: רבא: Sold for Theft, Not for Scheming
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects even the revised version. The Torah says a person is sold 'for his theft', which excludes being sold for scheming testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The Torah says 'And he shall be sold for his theft.' For his theft, and not for his scheming.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב המנונא completely, using a פסוק. עדים זוממין are never sold as an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בגנבתו' limits the sale to someone who actually stole. Witnesses who only schemed did not steal, so the sale never applies to them, whether they have money or not. This supports the ברייתא's rule with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One. A name for ה׳, used when quoting the Torah.
For his theft.
His scheming. The false plot of עדים זוממין.

steps.whatToRemember: עדים זוממין are never sold as an עבד עברי, because the Torah limits that sale to an actual thief ('בגנבתו').

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
'And he shall be sold for his theft,' the Torah said —
phrases.notes: שמות 22:2

phrases.english: for his theft, and not for his scheming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the revised version of רב המנונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both versions of רב המנונא entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah allows the sale only for real theft, not for scheming testimony.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עדים זוממין are never sold as an עבד עברי.

steps.title: Why Does רבי עקיבא Exempt Self-Admission?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's view in the ברייתא and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי עקיבא they said, etc. What is רבי עקיבא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא, where רבי עקיבא says עדים זוממין do not pay based on their own admission. It asks why, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person who admits he owes money must pay. So the גמרא wants to know why רבי עקיבא exempts witnesses who admit they were זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Etc. The rest of the quote is assumed.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Akiva they said, etc.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues: witnesses do not pay based on their own admission.

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Akiva's reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי עקיבא exempts witnesses who admit they were זוממין.

steps.title: Because It Is a Fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס, and a person does not pay a קנס based on his own admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds it is a fine, and a person does not pay a fine based on his own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: for רבי עקיבא, the payment is a fine, not repayment of a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a קנס is paid only when witnesses prove it, not when the person admits it. Since this payment is a קנס, admitting to being זוממין does not obligate payment.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine. A penalty set by the Torah, not repayment for actual damage.
Based on his own word, meaning by his own admission.
He holds. Introduces someone's reasoning.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the witnesses get off because they lied less. The reason is technical: a fine is never collected through self-admission.

phrases.english: He holds it is a fine,

phrases.aramaic: וּקְנָס אֵין מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: and one does not pay a fine based on his own admission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס, and a קנס is not paid on one's own admission.

steps.title: רבה: They Did Nothing, Yet Are Punished
steps.stepSummary: רבה shows it is a fine: the witnesses did no actual deed, yet they are executed or pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Know that it is a fine, for they did not do any action, and yet they are killed or they pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings support that the payment of עדים זוממין is really a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person is punished or pays only for an actual deed. The witnesses only spoke, and their plan never happened, yet they still get the punishment. A punishment without a real deed must be a fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it is so. Introduces a supporting proof.
An action, a deed.

phrases.english: Rabba said: Know that it is so,
for they did not do any action,
and yet they are killed or they pay.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. They're killed in a death case and pay in a money case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 33 that the payment is a קנס.
steps.raayaObject: That the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: They are punished even though they did no actual deed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: No Money Was Lost, Yet They Pay
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן shows it is a fine: the accused never lost any money, yet the witnesses pay him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Know that it is a fine, for the money is still with its owner, and yet they pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a second support that the payment is a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repayment for damage needs a real loss. Here the accused kept his money, because the false testimony was caught in time. Paying someone who lost nothing can only be a fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Money.
The owner. Here, the man the witnesses testified against.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס, so they do not pay based on their own admission. רבה and רב נחמן each give a reason it is a fine: there was no real deed, and there was no real loss.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Know that it is so,
for the money is still with its owner,
and yet they pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate support for the same claim as step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That the payment of עדים זוממין is a קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: They pay even though the accused never lost any money.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The payment of עדים זוממין is a fine, which explains רבי עקיבא's rule about self-admission.
